subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Matthews <ben.matthews@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 08 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Ben

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. If I missed anything important, tell me and I'll update.

Summary of what we heard
- Current stack: OpenAI (chat/completions + function calls) and Anthropic for some assistant flows; OpenAI embeddings (text-embedding-ada-002) for semantic search.
- Pain points:
  - Cost volatility and rising per-token spend on peak days
  - Rate limits and concurrency constraints impacting peak throughput
  - Vendor lock-in concerns for data residency and contractual terms
  - Auditability: need request-level logs and evidence for audits
  - Latency variability for real-time patient-facing features (target p50 < 300ms)
- Success criteria for migration:
  - Functional parity: streaming, function-calling semantics, and embedding vector compatibility
  - Performance: p50 latency <= 300ms for the critical chat endpoint in our environment
  - Cost: demonstrable per-unit cost reduction or clearer predictability vs current spend
  - Security/compliance: KMS integration, VPC/private deployment option, and audit logs for requests

Compatibility needs we tracked
- Tokenization and prompt compatibility for existing prompt/templating patterns
- Function-calling: ability to trigger and return structured JSON payloads identical to your current flow
- Embeddings: same dimensionality (or clear migration path) and near-zero drift for search quality
- Streaming API support for partial responses and cancellation

Initial model shortlist (we discussed approximate fit):
- Llama 2 (70B, quantized) - good general-purpose, widely tested
- Mistral-Instruct family - strong instruction following and cost-effective on GPU
- RedPajama / Falcon variants - candidate when we need open weights + fine-tuning
- Open-source embedding models (e.g., instructor-style or crowd-embeddings) - to validate search parity

Proposed next steps
1) Redwood POC: 6-week technical POC on Dedicated or Private deployment to validate latency, cost, and function-calling parity.
2) Tech deep-dive: schedule 60m session with your infra + security teams to review KMS, VPC, and audit log requirements (we recommended week of Aug 17).
3) Data & prompts intake: you to share 3 representative prompt+instruction sets and a small subset of recent traffic for benchmark replay (we will sign an NDA if needed).
4) Deliverables: migration checklist + draft SLA (attached), model shortlist with recommended quantization and cost estimates.

Attachments: redwood-migration-checklist.xlsx, redwood-sla-draft.pdf (high-level SLA + POC acceptance criteria)

Timeline & owners (high level)
- Week 0: kickoff + security deep-dive (Marissa / Rishi)
- Weeks 1-3: benchmark tests and small-scale replay (Aditya / Acme infra)
- Weeks 4-6: optimization, cost profiling, and handover to your platform team

Open questions for your team
- Can you share a rough monthly token/embedding volume (tokens per month, embedding calls per month)?
- Are there any strict model exclusions for regulatory/clinical reasons?
- Any internal SRE constraints around outbound network egress to a Redwood-managed endpoint vs Private deployment?

Thanks — I'll follow up here with calendar invites for the tech deep-dive + a link to the POC intake form.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Redwood Inference | Production-first inference for LLMs

From: Ben Matthews <ben.matthews@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 08 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Marissa, thanks for the thorough recap, very helpful. Confirming the items below and adding a few specifics from our side.

Confirmations / additional context
- Monthly usage: ~3B tokens (mix of prompts + completions), ~1.2M embedding calls/month. Peak concurrency around 90-120 simultaneous requests on weekdays.
- Current endpoints: chat/completions (OpenAI gpt-4o for complex assistant flows), Anthropic Claude for lower-latency conversational widgets. We use function-calling extensively for structured output that feeds downstream services.
- Latency SLOs: target p50 <= 300ms, p95 <= 900ms for the main chat endpoint, acceptable slippage during batch/off-peak is fine.
- Compliance: must be able to handle PHI under BAAs; we have in-house compliance controls and will need a KMS + audit logs solution.

Questions for Redwood
1) Function-calling parity: Do you support the same JSON-based function-calling contract and the ability to stream partial function outputs? Any known differences we should expect?
2) Embeddings compatibility: what open embedding models do you recommend to get within 95-98% similarity for our search use-case?
3) Cost estimate: can you share a back-of-envelope monthly cost projection for the POC (Dedicated pool) vs our current spend?

We're comfortable running the POC, assuming the cost case is compelling and you can meet the compliance requirements (KMS + audit logs + BAA path). Happy to do the tech deep-dive the week of Aug 17 — Tue/Wed afternoons work best.

Attaching our procurement checklist and high-level security questionnaire (procurement_procurement_checklist.pdf). I'll upload the larger security package if this moves to POC.

Thanks — I've copied our platform lead if any infra-specific details are needed.

Thanks Ben — great context and appreciate the procurement attachment. Quick follow-ups / confirms:

- Function-calling: Redwood supports JSON-based function calling with streaming of partial outputs; we will detail any surface differences in the tech deep-dive and provide a short compatibility shim if needed.
- Embeddings: initial recommendation is to test instructor-style open embedding models and a 1536-dim model we've validated; we'll include a similarity baseline in the POC.
- Cost estimate: we'll circulate a back-of-envelope for Dedicated POOL vs your current usage by EOD Mon (Aug 10).
- Tech deep-dive: tentatively scheduled Wed Aug 18 at 2pm PT — I'll send the calendar invite and include Rishi + Aditya from our side and your platform lead.

I've attached the migration checklist and draft SLA again and included a short POC intake form link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwoodAcmePOC — please drop the 3 prompt examples and a small traffic sample when convenient.
